title: 2B Reversal
teaches: The 2B bottom as we trade it: a stock breaks a prior swing low for the first time, goes no more than 3% under it and fails to follow through; the buy is a market order only after price trades back above the broken low, within 3 sessions, no more than 4% above it; the stop sits a few cents under the lowest low of the undercut, a close back under the broken low is a warning, a third comes off at 3R and 5R, and a market still making lower lows is not the place.

questions.q: Whose rule is the 2B?
choices: Victor Sperandeo
Larry Williams
T. Bulkowski
Linda Raschke
questions.answer: Victor Sperandeo
questions.why: Victor Sperandeo. Bulkowski's page credits him with the 2B pattern, from his book Trader Vic. The idea: in an uptrend, a higher high that fails to carry through is apt to reverse the trend. Bulkowski wrote the pattern up on his page. He did not originate it.
questions.lesson_line: The 2B is Sperandeo's rule: a break that fails.

wrong.Larry Williams: Bulkowski's page names Sperandeo as the source of the 2B, not Williams.
wrong.T. Bulkowski: Bulkowski wrote the pattern up on his page, but he credits Sperandeo with it.
wrong.Linda Raschke: The page that records the 2B credits Sperandeo, not Raschke.

questions.simple: Victor Sperandeo. Bulkowski's page credits him with the 2B, a break of a prior low or high that fails.

reasons: +3 the credit rests on one web page (Bulkowski's, quoting Sperandeo's book)

questions.q: A 2B bottom breaks a prior low, then fails and closes back above it.
questions.answer: True
questions.why: True. A 2B bottom is a first break under a prior low that goes no more than 3% under it, fails to follow through and closes back above it. In Bulkowski's words the right valley sits below the left. With no close back above within 3 sessions it is a breakdown, not a 2B.
questions.lesson_line: A 2B is a break that fails. It dips under the low and reclaims it.
questions.simple: True. A 2B is a break under a prior low that fails fast and closes back above it.

reasons: +2 the 3% depth line and the 3-session window are the card's proposed criteria

questions.q: When can you buy a 2B bottom?
choices: Once it trades back above the low
As soon as it undercuts the low
On the second undercut of that low
After three closes under the low
questions.answer: Once it trades back above the low
questions.why: After it trades back above the broken low. Never before the reclaim. Buying the undercut itself is guessing. Sperandeo's trigger is the return through the level, and our entry is a market order. With no close back above within 3 sessions it is a breakdown, not a 2B.
questions.lesson_line: Wait for the reclaim. The undercut alone is not a trigger.

wrong.As soon as it undercuts the low: Buying the break before the reclaim is a named mistake.
wrong.On the second undercut of that low: The first break is the one that counts. A second undercut is not the trigger.
wrong.After three closes under the low: No close back above the broken low within 3 sessions makes it a breakdown, not a 2B.

questions.simple: Wait until the stock trades back above the broken low. Buying the undercut itself is a guess.

deeper.trap: At the undercut you cannot yet tell a 2B from a breakdown. With no close back above the broken low within 3 sessions it is a breakdown, not a 2B. The reclaim is what turns the guess into a trigger.

reasons: +2 keyed through the card's proposed 'never before the reclaim' while the trigger rule is held (D-003)

questions.q: You buy the 2B as soon as the low breaks, before any reclaim.
questions.answer: False
questions.why: False. We never buy before the reclaim. Buying the undercut itself is guessing. The trigger is the return through the broken low, as Sperandeo has it. Until price trades back above, a break can still turn out to be a plain breakdown, not a 2B.
questions.lesson_line: No reclaim, no trade. Buying the undercut is guessing.
questions.simple: False. Buying the break is guessing, so we wait until price trades back above the broken low.

deeper.trap: The undercut can look like a bargain, and buying it feels early and smart. Our card names it as a mistake: buying the break before the reclaim. Waiting costs a little price. It spares you a break that never reclaims, which is a breakdown and not a 2B.

reasons: fixed before: re-keyed off a Bulkowski misreading

questions.q: What is a 2B bottom, in one line?
choices: A failed first break of a swing low
A gap down that reclaims the prior close
A 2 ATR flush on 2x volume at a low
A dip under a rising 50-day, then back
questions.answer: A failed first break of a swing low
questions.why: A failed first break of a prior swing low. It goes no more than 3% under the low and fails to follow through. An Oops is judged on yesterday's low. A U&R is judged on a level such as a rising 50-day. A capitulation is a 2 ATR flush on 2x volume.
questions.lesson_line: A 2B is a failed break of a swing low.

wrong.A gap down that reclaims the prior close: That is the Oops, judged on yesterday's low.
wrong.A 2 ATR flush on 2x volume at a low: That is a capitulation, a different setup.
wrong.A dip under a rising 50-day, then back: A rising average as the level makes it a U&R.

questions.simple: A 2B is the first break under a prior swing low that fails fast and goes back above it.

deeper.trap: The shape looks the same, so name the level first. A swing low at least 5 sessions old is a 2B. Yesterday's low is an Oops. A rising 20 EMA or 50-day, a prior high, a round number or the 10-session range low is a U&R.

reasons: +2 the look-alike tells are the card's proposed criteria

Far from any moving average
Far under the 200-day
Right after a big red news bar

questions.simple: True. After you buy, a trade under the new low is your exit, and you take it at once.

questions.q: 2B or Oops?
choices: An Oops, the low is one day old
A 2B, it reclaimed on the same day
A breakdown, it broke a low
A spring, it closed back inside
questions.story: Yesterday closed at 83.20 with a low of 82.40. Today opens at 82.70, trades down to 82.10 and closes at 83.60.
questions.answer: An Oops, the low is one day old
questions.why: An Oops. Today opened at 82.70, under the prior close of 83.20. It broke yesterday's low of 82.40 and closed at 83.60, back over the prior close. A 2B breaks a swing low at least 5 sessions old. Yesterday's low is one session old.
questions.lesson_line: Count the age of the broken low. One day old is an Oops.

wrong.A 2B, it reclaimed on the same day: A 2B breaks a swing low at least 5 sessions old. This broke yesterday's low.
wrong.A breakdown, it broke a low: It closed back above the low it broke. A breakdown has no close back above within 3 sessions.
wrong.A spring, it closed back inside: A spring's level is the floor of a sideways range of 15 sessions or more. This broke yesterday's low.

questions.simple: An Oops. It opened under the prior close, broke yesterday's low and reclaimed the prior close, and a 2B needs an older low.

deeper.trap: The shape looks like a 2B, so check the age of the low and the open. An Oops opens under the prior close and breaks yesterday's low. A 2B breaks a swing low at least 5 sessions old. Calling any dip under yesterday's low a 2B is a named mistake.

reasons: +2 rests on the card's proposed look-alike tell (Oops)

questions.q: 2B or Oops?
choices: A 2B, it broke an older swing low
An Oops, it reclaimed a prior close
A Remount, it was slow to reclaim
A spring, it closed back inside
questions.story: On Tuesday the stock breaks a swing low made twelve sessions ago. It closes back above that low on Wednesday.
questions.answer: A 2B, it broke an older swing low
questions.why: A 2B. The broken low is twelve sessions old, older than the 5 sessions a 2B needs. The close back above came the next day, inside 3 sessions. An Oops breaks yesterday's low and reclaims the prior close the same day.
questions.lesson_line: An older swing low and a reclaim in a day or two: that is a 2B.

wrong.An Oops, it reclaimed a prior close: An Oops breaks yesterday's low and reclaims the prior close the same day.
wrong.A Remount, it was slow to reclaim: A Remount follows five or more closes under the level.
wrong.A spring, it closed back inside: A spring's level is the floor of a sideways range of 15 sessions or more, not a single swing low.

questions.simple: A 2B. The broken low is twelve sessions old and the stock closed back above it the next day.

deeper.trap: Two tests separate the look-alikes: how old is the broken low, and how many closes under before the reclaim. Twelve sessions old and a close back above the next day passes both. An Oops needs yesterday's low. A Remount needs five or more closes under.

reasons: +2 rests on the card's proposed look-alike tells (Oops, Remount)

questions.q: 2B or Oops?
choices: A 2B, the low is not yesterday's
An Oops, it reclaimed the same day
A Remount, it retook an old low
A breakdown, it dipped under a low
questions.story: The stock opens above yesterday's close. It dips under a swing low made thirteen sessions ago and closes back above it the same day.
questions.answer: A 2B, the low is not yesterday's
questions.why: A 2B. An Oops opens under the prior close and is judged on yesterday's low. This stock opened above yesterday's close and broke a swing low thirteen sessions old, older than the 5 sessions a 2B needs. It closed back above the same day, well inside 3 sessions.
questions.lesson_line: The open and the reference low decide it. Old swing low, 2B.

wrong.An Oops, it reclaimed the same day: An Oops opens under the prior close. This one opened above it.
wrong.A Remount, it retook an old low: A Remount needs five or more closes under the level.
wrong.A breakdown, it dipped under a low: It closed back above the low the same day. A breakdown has no close back above within 3 sessions.

questions.simple: A 2B. It opened above yesterday's close and broke an older swing low, so it is not an Oops.

deeper.trap: Do not label by the dip alone. The open decides whether it can be an Oops: an Oops opens under the prior close and is judged on yesterday's low. This stock opened above yesterday's close and broke a swing low thirteen sessions old, so the label is 2B.

reasons: +2 rests on the card's proposed look-alike tell (Oops)

questions.q: 2B or U&R?
choices: A U&R, the level is an average
A 2B, it reclaimed the line
An Oops, it dipped and recovered
A Remount, it retook the average
questions.story: A leader dips under its rising 50-day average and closes back above it. There was no swing low nearby.
questions.answer: A U&R, the level is an average
questions.why: A U&R. When the level is a rising average, a prior high, a round number or the range low, it is a U&R. A 2B breaks a swing low. Here the level was the rising 50-day and there was no swing low nearby.
questions.lesson_line: Name the level. A swing low is a 2B. A rising average is a U&R.

wrong.A 2B, it reclaimed the line: A 2B breaks a prior swing low, not an average.
wrong.An Oops, it dipped and recovered: An Oops needs a break of yesterday's low.
wrong.A Remount, it retook the average: A Remount follows five or more closes under a level. This leader dipped under and closed back above.

questions.simple: A U&R. The level was a rising average, and a 2B breaks a swing low.

deeper.trap: Name the level before the label. A rising 20 EMA or 50-day, a prior high, a round number or the 10-session range low makes it a U&R. A swing low at least 5 sessions old makes it a 2B. The dip and the reclaim look the same, so the level is the tell.

reasons: +2 the level test is the card's tb.level criterion, still held (D-101)
+1 rests on one card line

questions.q: 2B or Remount?
choices: A Remount, bought on the retake
A 2B, it reclaimed the broken low
An Oops, it reclaimed the prior close
A spring, it retook the floor
questions.story: The stock closed under an old low for six sessions. Today it trades back above that low.
questions.answer: A Remount, bought on the retake
questions.why: A Remount. A 2B closes back above within 3 sessions, and five or more closes under it is a Remount, bought on the retake of the line. GS on 2017-01-25 had 6 closes under the 236.64 low before the first close back above.
questions.lesson_line: Count the closes under the line. Five or more is a Remount.

wrong.A 2B, it reclaimed the broken low: A 2B closes back above within 3 sessions. Six closes under is too long.
wrong.An Oops, it reclaimed the prior close: An Oops reclaims the prior close the same day and is judged on yesterday's low. This stayed under for six closes.
wrong.A spring, it retook the floor: A spring closes back inside the same day or the next. This stayed under for six closes.

questions.simple: A Remount. Six closes under the line is too many for a 2B, which must close back above within 3 sessions.

deeper.trap: The count of closes under the line is the tell. A 2B closes back above within 3 sessions. Five or more closes under, then a retake, is a Remount, bought on the retake of the line, not on the reclaim of a low.

reasons: +2 the reclaim-window grading is held (D-102)
+1 rests on one dossier example

questions.q: 2B or a spring?
choices: A spring, the level is a floor
A 2B, it reclaimed a swing low
An Oops, it closed back inside
A Remount, it retook the floor
questions.story: A stock has traded sideways for 20 sessions and touched its floor three times. It dips under the floor and closes back inside the same day.
questions.answer: A spring, the level is a floor
questions.why: A spring. A spring's level is the floor of a sideways range of 15 sessions or more, touched at least twice, with the close back inside the same day or the next. This stock traded sideways for 20 sessions and touched its floor three times. A 2B breaks a single swing low.
questions.lesson_line: A range floor is a spring. A single swing low is a 2B.

wrong.A 2B, it reclaimed a swing low: A 2B's level is a single swing low, not the floor of a range.
wrong.An Oops, it closed back inside: An Oops is judged on yesterday's low.
wrong.A Remount, it retook the floor: A Remount follows five or more closes under the level. This closed back inside the same day.

questions.simple: A spring. The level is the floor of a long sideways range, not a single swing low.

deeper.trap: A spring and a 2B look alike on a chart, so the level tells them apart. A spring's level is the floor of a sideways range of 15 sessions or more, touched at least twice. A 2B breaks a single swing low.

reasons: +2 the level test is the card's tb.level criterion, still held (D-101)
+1 rests on one card line

questions.q: Is it a 2B?
choices: No, no prior swing low to break
Yes, it dipped under and reclaimed
Yes, it is a Remount of the low
No, it needs a gap down first
questions.story: A stock falls for six days in a row. Today it dips under yesterday's low and closes a little higher.
questions.answer: No, no prior swing low to break
questions.why: No. A one-day dip under yesterday's low is an Oops, not a 2B: the level must be at least 5 sessions old. In a six-day decline each low is only a day old, so there is no prior swing low to break. Calling any dip under yesterday's low a 2B is a named mistake.
questions.lesson_line: Calling any dip under yesterday's low a 2B is a mistake.

wrong.Yes, it dipped under and reclaimed: A dip under yesterday's low is not a 2B.
wrong.Yes, it is a Remount of the low: A Remount follows five or more closes under a level.
wrong.No, it needs a gap down first: The open does not decide it. The level does: a 2B breaks a swing low at least 5 sessions old.

questions.simple: No. Yesterday's low is only one day old, and a 2B needs a swing low at least 5 sessions old.

deeper.trap: Calling any dip under yesterday's low a 2B is a named mistake. In a straight decline every low is only a day old. The level must be at least 5 sessions old, and a one-day dip under yesterday's low is an Oops, not a 2B.

reasons: +2 rests on the card's proposed look-alike tell (age of the level)

questions.q: Is it a 2B?
choices: No, it is not the first break
Yes, it reclaimed the low
Yes, a second try looks stronger
No, the reclaim came too fast
questions.story: Last week the stock traded under a swing low and bounced. This week it dips under the same low again and closes back above it.
questions.answer: No, it is not the first break
questions.why: No. The break must be the first session to trade under the low since it formed. Last week's bounce already used it, so this dip and reclaim is not a 2B. A reclaim after a second break does not make it stronger.
questions.lesson_line: Only the first break of the low counts.

wrong.Yes, it reclaimed the low: The reclaim is not enough. The break must be the first.
wrong.No, the reclaim came too fast: A close back above within 3 sessions is what a 2B asks for. Speed is not the problem. The first-break test is.

questions.simple: No. Only the first break of the low counts, and this was a second try.

deeper.trap: A second try can feel stronger, but only the first break counts. The break must be the first session to trade under that low since it formed. A market still making lower lows with no reclaim is not the place for a 2B either.

reasons: +2 rests on the card's proposed first-break criterion

questions.q: Which rule fails?
choices: The undercut was too deep
The swing low was too recent
It was slow to close back above
It was not the first break
questions.story: A stock breaks, for the first time, a swing low made 15 sessions ago. It closes back above that low within 3 sessions. The lowest low of the undercut went 4.36% under the old low.
questions.answer: The undercut was too deep
questions.why: The undercut was too deep. The lowest low of the undercut must be no more than 3% under the prior low, so the stop fits. DELL on 2024-07-22 went 4.36% under its 127.59 low, and the stop that followed was 4.83% from the entry. A deeper break that closes back above is not a 2B at full size.
questions.lesson_line: A deep undercut is not a 2B at full size.

wrong.The swing low was too recent: At 15 sessions old the low is well past the 5-session line.
wrong.It was slow to close back above: It closed back above within 3 sessions, inside the window.
wrong.It was not the first break: The story says it was the first break.

questions.simple: The undercut. It went 4.36% under the old low, and a 2B must stay within 3%.

deeper.trap: A close back above is not enough. The undercut must also be shallow. DELL closed back above its 127.59 low, but only after a 4.36% undercut, so the stop that followed was 4.83% from the entry. That is not a 2B at full size.

reasons: +2 the dossier numbers are read off our own bars

The low was too old

wrong.The gap was too big: The gap is not the failing number.
wrong.The low was too old: Age is not the failing number.
wrong.The break was too shallow: A shallow break is what we want.

questions.simple: The close is under the 200-day average. We take no longs below it, so this one is watch only.

The reclaim day closed near the high

The undercut was too deep
The reclaim day closed low
The low was too young

It proves the 2B will keep running
It removes the need for a stop
It tells you to sell the whole trade

questions.q: Hidden ticker, today. It undercut a swing low and closed back above it. Which statement fits the chart?

The reclaim took five sessions to land
The broken low was only one day old

Take it; the gap shows strength
Take it; the low is old

questions.why: The low it broke is only a day old. An Oops breaks yesterday's low and reclaims the prior close the same day. A 2B breaks a swing low at least 5 sessions old.
